topic_text: The value of goods and services produced in the UK.
text:
UK gross domestic product (GDP) shows an estimated fall of 0.2% in Quarter 3 (July to Sept) 2022. There was a slowing on the quarter for the services, production and construction industries; likely because of energy price rises affecting household disposable incomes.

It is important to note that data for September 2022 (and a lesser extent the Quarter 3 estimates) are affected by the bank holiday for the State Funeral of Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II, where some businesses operated differently on this day.

topic_text: How much the production and services industries contribute to economic output.
text:
Monthly production output rose by 0.2% between August and September 2022 and is now 0.3% above February 2020, which was the last month of “normal” trading conditions prior to the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

Output remained below the February 2020 pre-coronavirus pandemic levels in two of the four production sectors, with monthly mining and quarrying output 13.5% below and manufacturing 1.5% below the February 2020 level; in contrast, water supply and sewerage was 13.9%, and electricity and gas 10.6% above the February 2020 level.

Monthly services output fell by 0.8% between August and September 2022 and is now 0.6% below February 2020, which was the last month of “normal” trading conditions prior to the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The Index of Services (IoS) saw falls in 9 of the 14 sectors during September 2022; most notably information and communication seeing the largest fall, contributing negative 0.29 percentage points to IoS (with growth falling by 3.2%).

topic_text: Measures of demand in the economy for output that is produced.
text: Retail sales volumes fell by 0.5% in May 2022 following a rise of 0.4% in April 2022 sales volumes were 2.6% above their pre-coronavirus (COVID-19) February 2020 levels.

Business investment fell by 0.5% in Quarter 3 (July to Sept) 2022.

The level of business investment in Quarter 3 2022 is 8.4% below where it was in Quarter 4 (Oct to Dec) 2019, the quarter before the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic; gross fixed capital formation (GFCF) levels are 0.8% above that same quarter.

topic_text: Demand and supply of labour in the economy and how much employees earn.
text: The employment rate was estimated at 75.5% for July to September 2022, 0.1 percentage points up on the year but unchanged on the quarter.
The unemployment rate was estimated at 3.6% for July to September 2022, 0.7 percentage points down on the year and 0.2 percentage points down on the quarter.

Average weekly earnings for employees in Great Britain in nominal terms (not adjusted for inflation) increased by 6.0% for total pay (including bonuses) and 5.7% for regular pay (excluding bonuses) in July to September 2022.

topic_text: Changes in prices of goods and services bought by consumers, as well as those bought and sold by producers in the UK.
text:
The Consumer Prices Index including owner occupiers' housing costs (CPIH) 12-month inflation rate was 8.6% in August 2022, down from 8.8% in July 2022.

Consumer price inflation can be influenced by the strength of domestic supply and demand and also changes in the UK prices of imports. The inflation rate also depends on price levels in the preceding year.

Producer output (factory gate) prices rose by 16.5% in the year to June 2022, up from 15.8% in the year to May 2022.

Changes in the output Producer Price Index inflation rate can be influenced by changes in labour and energy costs.

Producer input prices rose by 24.0% in the year to June 2022, up from 22.4% in the year to May 2022.

Input prices are influenced by raw material prices and exchange rate movements so are more changeable over time.

topic_text: UK exports and imports of goods and services and measures of foreign direct investment.
text:
Total imports of goods, excluding precious metals, decreased by £2.8 billion (5.0%) in September 2022, with imports from EU countries decreasing by £1.9 billion (7.3%) and imports from non-EU countries falling by £0.9 billion (3.0%).

The decrease in imports from non-EU countries was primarily driven by a £1.3 billion decrease in fuel imports, linked to falling gas imports from Norway and falling oil prices during September.

Total exports of goods, excluding precious metals, decreased by £1.6 billion (4.7%) in September 2022, with exports to EU countries falling by £0.9 billion (5.1%) and exports to non-EU countries decreasing by £0.7 billion (4.2%).

Removing the effect of inflation, total imports of goods, excluding previous metals, decreased by £2.6 billion (6.1%) and total exports of goods, excluding precious metals, decreased by £1.4 billion (4.8%) in September 2022.

Total imports of services remained at £19.1 billion in September 2022 and total exports of services also remained flat at £31.6 billion.

Removing the effect of inflation, total imports and exports of services remained at a similar levels to August 2022.

The total trade in goods and services deficit, excluding precious metals, narrowed by £1.3 billion to £23.7 billion in Quarter 3 (July to Sept), but has remained relatively unchanged over the past three quarters.

Removing the effect of inflation, the total trade deficit, excluding precious metals, narrowed by £8.1 billion to £8.7 billion in Quarter 3 2022.

bulletin_title: Foreign direct investment involving UK companies
text: UK direct investment liabilities were £1,287.6 billion in April to June 2016, up slightly from £1,272.4 billion in the previous quarter. FDI liabilities were following a broadly upward trend in previous years, before falling in January to March 2016.

bulletin_title: Foreign direct investment involving UK companies
text: UK direct investment assets were £1,414.7 billion in April to June 2016, up from £1,349.5 billion in the previous quarter. The value of FDI liabilities has fluctuated over the past two years, although remains broadly similar to levels seen in 2012.
